FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 4 1 ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalised by the Methods of Chemical Analysis of Ores, Minerals and Allied Materials for Metallurgical Industry Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. IS 1917 : 1962 `Methods of chemical analysis of quartzite and high silica sand' covers the methods for the determination of silica and other constituents of quartzite and high silica sand. The Committee decided to revise this standard into different parts and covering determination of each element in a separate part, which on publication would supersede the determination of that element given in IS 1917 : 1962. The determination of loss on ignition, silica, sodium, potassium, aluminium, iron, calcium, magnesium and titanium oxide in quartzite and high silica sand have been covered in this series. This part covers the determination Part 1 Determination Part 2 Part 3 Part 5 Part 6 Part 7 Determination Determination Determination Determination Determination of aluminium. The other parts in this series are;

of loss on ignition of sodium and potassium of silica of iron of calcium and magnesium of titania and `The difference method'

In this revision, the determination of alumina by the `Oxine method' has been replaced by atomic absorption spectrometric method.

In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised Y.

3.1 The sample shall be drawn and prepared after quartering in accordance with IS 2245 : 1962 or Es 1811 : 1984, as the case may be. 3.2 Grind 3 to 5 g of the sample ( 3.1 ) so that it passes through IS Test Sieve No. 15 ( 149 microns ). Dry the sample in a weighing tube at 105" to 110�C for 2 hours. Keep the tube stoppered in a desiccator and cool to room temperature. 4 QUALITY OF REAGFNTS Unless specified otherwise, analytical grade reagents and distilled water (. see IS 1070 : 19'77 ) shall be employed for the test. 5 DETERMINATION OF ALUMINIUM

5.4 Procedure 5.4.1 Test Portion Weigh to the nearest 0'001 g, 2'0 g of the sample ( 3.2 ). Transfer it to a platinum crucib e. 5.4.2 Dissolution of the Test Portion 5.4.2.1 Moisten with 2 ml of water and add 10 ml of hydrofluoric acid ( 40 percent ) and 1 ml of dilute sulphuric acid ( 1 : 1 >. Warm on a hot plate with the lid till the sample is decomposed. Remove the lid and evaporate slowly to fumes. Cool the dish and wash the inner sides of the dish with little water, add further 5 ml of hydrofluoric acid and evaporate on hot plate to dryness. Fuse the residue with 1 g of potassium bisulphate

5.1 Outline of the Method The sample is decomposed by hydrofluorization andthe residue fused with potassium bisulphate and dissolved in hydrochloric acid. Alumina is determined at 309 nm by atomic absorption spectrophotometer. 5.2 Reagents 5.2.1 Hydrojluoric Acid, 40 percent ( m/v ) 5.2.2 Dilute Sulphuric Acid, I : 1 ( V/V).

slowly to a clear melt. Cool and extract the melt with 10 to 15 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid ( 1 : 1 ). Boil the extracted mass to get a clear solution, cool and make up to 250 ml in a calibrated volumetric flask. 5.4.2.2 Take an appropriate aliquot of the solution ( 5.4.2.1) in a 100 ml flask. ( For sample containing less than 0'5 percent alumina, no dilution is necessary ). Add 10 percent calculated amount of potassium chloride solution into it
NOTES 1 2 ml of 10 percent KCI in 100 ml volume contains 1000 p.g / ml of potassium. 2 If sufficient sodium or potassium salt is present in the solution, further addition is not required.

repeatedly to ensure that there is no drift of absorbance. Finally aspirate water and set the absorbance to zero reading. 5.4.5 Atomic Absorption Measurement
5.4.5.1 Aspirate first the blank solution and then the calibration solution in increasing order, aspirating water between each aspiration of the solution and record the absorbance reading. Then aspirate the test sample and note the absorbance. Each aspiration should be made at least three times and take the average value. Solids which builds up on the burner slit must be removed, otherwise they will cause a decrease of sensitivity. 5.4.5.2 Deduct the blank value from the absorbance of the standard as well as the test solution.

5.4.5.3 Prepare a calibration curve by plotting the absorbance value of the standard solutions against the concentration in the pg / ml of the element. 5.4.5.4 Compute the concentration of the test solution ( corrected for the blank ) to yg of .the element per ml from the calibration curve. 5.4.6 Calculation Calculate the percentage of aluminium content as follows: . Follow the instructions of the manufacturer in preparing the instrument. Switch on the instrument and the aluminium hollow cathode lamp. Fit the correct burner for nitrous oxide-acetylene flame and light the appropriate flame ( lean ). Wait for about 20 minutes for stablization. Set the wave length at 309 nm. Optimize instrument response by adjusting the wavelength, fuel, an, burner and nebulizer while aspirating the highest calibration solution. As the sensitivity varies from instrument to instrument the concentration of the standard series and of the test solution should be adjusted accordingly. At the same time check the linearity of the calibration curve. Aspirate water and one of the calibration solution

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
